Me gusta crear soluciones útiles, aprender nuevas herramientas y trabajar en equipo. Busco un grupo comprometido, creativo y multidisciplinario para competir en NASA Space Apps 2026. 🚀
summary: Choosing what to plant next in Peru’s Chira Valley depends on variable rainfall, limited irrigation water, and the crops already growing on a plot. AgroOrbit Perú is a decision-support prototype that brings those factors together. It shows daily NASA POWER records from 2016 to 2026 alongside dated MODIS Terra satellite imagery and lets users enter crop history, water availability, and priorities. When data are incomplete, the app identifies the gaps. An illustrative scenario then compares a reference rotation and two alternatives across two growing seasons, with dates, trade-offs, and sources. This gives farmers and advisers a concrete starting point for discussing crop choices and deciding what evidence to gather before planting.
details:
AgroOrbit Perú is a web prototype for exploring crop rotations in the Chira Valley, Sullana, Piura. A user locates a plot, records the previous and current crops, enters the next planting date and water availability, and chooses a priority such as saving water or improving soil.

We used NASA Earthdata Search to find and access Earth observation data for the project. The map shows the plot marker inside the regional NASA POWER grid cell and adds optional dated MODIS Terra imagery from NASA GIBS. Seeing the marker and grid together makes the difference in scale visible. The dashboard uses NASA POWER air temperature, precipitation, and modeled surface and root-zone soil wetness. Historical ranges show how conditions have varied across years. The dashboard displays ESP32 soil-temperature and moisture readings separately as hardware test data collected outside the field.

The Chira Valley demonstration

Starting on December 1, 2026, the demo compares a projected maize → cowpea reference with two alternatives, cowpea → sweet potato and sweet potato → cowpea. Changing the order changes when each crop would be in the field and which crop follows the current cowpea. Each option shows campaign dates, trade-offs, limitations, and sources. The dates and loam texture are illustrative, and the scores are synthetic test values. A field evaluation would require local soil and irrigation data and validated agronomic rules.

Why this matters

The prototype gives farmers and extension teams a way to discuss which crop sequence to explore, surface the assumptions shaping the comparison, and identify what to measure before making a planting decision.

How we built it.

The web app uses React and TypeScript with Leaflet and Recharts. The API uses Python and FastAPI. Supabase provides authentication and PostgreSQL storage. An ESP32 kit demonstrates measurement ingestion, with the frontend deployed on Vercel and the API on Render. The public repository includes the documented demo scenarios and instructions to reproduce them.

Live web app — https://agroorbit-three.vercel.app/
